title: SangerTools Vignette
text: package created provide convenient functions working population health data. specifically aimed healthcare providers services focus population health management. Many functions centered around Master Patient Index format. row patient column observation patient. next sections take use tool.

title: SangerTools Vignette
text: load Master Patient Index attached SangerTools package follow steps: data contains: PseudoNHSNumber - Pseudonymised NHS Patient Identifier Sex - identifiable sex patient Smoker - Health Condition Flag: 1 denotes patient smoker Diabetes - Health Condition Flag: 1 denotes patient diabetes Dementia - Health Condition Flag: 1 denotes patient dementia Obesity - Health Condition Flag: 1 denotes patient Obese Age - Age patient IMD_Decile - decile indices multiple deprivation Ethnicity - identifiable ethnicity patient} Locality - region patient lives - sampled Gloucestershire Clinical Commissioning Group (GCCG) PrimaryCareNetwork - network General Practioners patient registered - sampled (GCCG) data can start work function package.
code: health_data <- SangerTools::master_patient_index

title: SangerTools Vignette
text: common practice transform continuous age values smaller set categories. two functions package . age_bandizer age_bandizer2 age_bandizer Uses tidyverse philosophy function creation Non-Standard Evaluation. produce new column 5 year age bands factor. age_bandizer2 uses Standard Evaluation currently takes puts band size 2,5,10 & 20.
code: health_data <- SangerTools::age_bandizer(df = health_data,                                          Age_col = Age)  health_data <- SangerTools::age_bandizer_2(df = health_data,                                            Age_col = "Age",                                            Age_band_size = 5)

what: Generating a categorical column chart easily
title: SangerTools Vignette
text: package makes simple create categorical column chart. implemented next example:   really simple generate nice looking proportional charts.
code: # Group by Ethnicity diabetes_df <- health_data %>%    dplyr::filter(Diabetes==1)      SangerTools::categorical_col_chart(df = diabetes_df,                                      grouping_var = Ethnicity)+   scale_fill_sanger()+    labs(title = "Diabetic Patients by Ethnicity",        subtitle = "Nearly All Diabetics are White",        x = NULL,         y = "Number of Patients") +    coord_flip() # Group by Sex health_data %>%    dplyr::filter(Diabetes==1) %>%    SangerTools::categorical_col_chart(Sex) +    scale_fill_sanger()+   labs(title = "Diabetic Patients by Gender",        x = NULL,         y = "Number of Patients")

title: SangerTools Vignette
text: look crude rate diabetes obtain crude prevalence rate, can achieved :
code: crude_prevalence <- SangerTools::crude_rates(df = health_data,                                               Condition =  Diabetes,                                                Locality) #> Joining with `by = join_by(Locality)`

title: SangerTools Vignette
text: Let’s revisit example . Diabetes highly confounded age. diabetics diagnosed age 40. Given Localities now population structure county whole; can see slight differences crude prevalence rates.
code: asr_prevalence <- SangerTools::standardised_rates_df(df = health_data,                                    Split_by = Locality,                                    Condition = Diabetes,                                     Population_Standard = NULL,                                    Granular = FALSE,                                    Ageband ) #> Joining with `by = join_by(Locality, Ageband)` #> Joining with `by = join_by(Ageband)`

what: Age Standardised Rates with User Defined Population Structure
title: SangerTools Vignette
text: use another dataset attached package; UK population year 2018. broken 5 year age bands. user define population structure integrate standardised_rates_df ensure change name population column Pop_Weight

title: SangerTools Vignette
code: uk_pop18<- SangerTools::uk_pop_standard  names(uk_pop18) <- c("Pop_Weight","Ageband")

title: SangerTools Vignette
code: asr_uk <- SangerTools::standardised_rates_df(df = health_data,                                    Split_by = Locality,                                    Condition = Diabetes,                                     Population_Standard = uk_pop18,                                    Granular = FALSE,                                    Ageband ) #> Joining with `by = join_by(Locality, Ageband)` #> Joining with `by = join_by(Ageband)`

title: SangerTools Vignette
text: view crude standardised rates can use dplyr::left_join functionality added package use multiple CSV reader clipboard functions.
code: combined_rates <- crude_prevalence %>%    dplyr::left_join(asr_prevalence, by = c("Locality"))

title: SangerTools Vignette
text: copies data frame clipboard pasting Excel sheets, csvs, raw text. potential read multiple CSVs well can fed data frames.
code: SangerTools::excel_clip(combined_rates)

title: SangerTools Vignette
text: implement function need number CSVs contained folder. read , follow instructions: multiple_excel_reader equivalent excel files; however please read function documentation page functions strict set requirements execute.
code: file_path = 'my_file_path_where_csvs_are_stored'  if (length(SangerTools::multiple_csv_reader(file_path))==0){   message("This won't work without changing the variable input to a local file path with CSVs in") } #> This won't work without changing the variable input to a local file path with CSVs in

title: SangerTools Vignette
text: split_and_save quick way split dataframe specified column subsequent dataframes dataframes dynamically written location choice
code: SangerTools::split_and_save(  df = health_data,  Split_by = "Locality",  file_path = "Inputs/",  prefix = NULL )

title: SangerTools Vignette
text: Write results SQL Server ensuring table name appears expected. function makes number assumptions limited scope; please read documentation.
code: SangerTools::df_to_sql(df = combined_rates,                        driver = "SQL SERVER",                        server = "Org-sql-db",                        database = "MyReports",                        sql_table_name = "Diabetes_Prevalence",                        overwrite = FALSE)

title: SangerTools 1.0.3
text: Added testthat (edition 3) test suite covering every exported function bundled dataset. code changes exported functions; tests document current behaviour protect regressions. Expanded GitHub Actions R-CMD-check workflow matrix {macOS, Windows, Ubuntu} x {R-release, R-devel, R-oldrel-1}. Added test-coverage workflow (covr + Codecov) pkgdown workflow builds deploys https://ald0405.github.io/SangerTools/ push master. Added new vignette, demo-data--functions, walks three bundled datasets exercises every exported function one notebook. Documented df_to_sql() targets Microsoft SQL Server via ODBC Windows integrated security (behaviour unchanged). Removed dead AppVeyor badge README.md; added Codecov, pkgdown, lifecycle R-CMD-check badges. Bumped declared minimum R version 2.10 3.5.0 match current CRAN policy dependencies actually used. Refreshed RoxygenNote 7.3.2.
